subject: Acme Health - rate cap misconfiguration causing 429 spikes & retry storms
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-eng@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Elevated 429s and downstream timeouts - urgent help needed

Stephanie,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and a downstream retry storm starting around 08:45 PT this morning. Our customer-facing endpoints are timing out (15-25s) and the frontend is seeing cascading retries which amplifies the error rate. Attached is a trimmed log snippet showing the 429 burst and client retry timestamps (acme_429-log-snippet.txt).

Impact: several production customers reported degraded UX; we're tracking at least a 20% drop in successful responses for the payments flow. We do not have any code changes on our side.

Can you confirm whether this is a quota/rate-limit change or something on Redwood's side? We need a short RCA and mitigation steps now.

—Jordan
Platform Ops, Acme Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 429s and downstream timeouts - urgent help needed

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. We're investigating with our SRE and quota teams immediately. Early question: are you on the Standard tier or Enterprise reserved capacity for this org/project? That helps us check tiering policies.

I'll loop in Rishi for triage and Marcus for escalation if this needs exec attention. We'll aim to provide a mitigation within 30 minutes and a follow-up with detailed steps.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll treat this as high priority.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): acme_429-log-snippet.txt

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 429s and downstream timeouts - urgent help needed

Jordan / Stephanie —

Initial triage update:
- We see a sudden spike in 429s originating from your org.project: acme-health.prod (org ID 0x4b3). 429s started at 08:43:12 PT and correlate with a batch of retries from your frontends.
- Root cause (preliminary): a recent change in our rate-tier mapping accidentally moved one of your projects from the Enterprise reserved pool into the Shared Standard tier for a short window due to a misapplied org-level override. That triggered a much lower per-project token throughput (org-level limits) and exposed your traffic to global throttling.
- There are also many client-side retry attempts with exponential backoff disabled, which amplified the load into a retry storm.

Mitigations performed (~10:00 PT):
1) We reverted the tier mapping for acme-health.prod to the Enterprise pool (now back at committed throughput) — immediate reduction in 429s observed.
2) Temporarily raised the per-project rate cap for the org to match previous committed rates while we validate configs.
3) We disabled a misbehaving autoscaling throttle that was enforcing conservative burst limits during the re-mapping.

I've attached the quota-config-snapshot.png and a CSV of retry counts for your engineering review. Next steps: we'll run a careful audit of all org-level overrides, push a patch to the tier mapping service to prevent the incorrect override, and coordinate a post-incident review.

Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): quota-config-snapshot.png, acme_retry-matrix.csv

From: Tina Rodriguez <tina.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: platform-eng@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 429s and downstream timeouts - urgent help needed

Thanks for the fast response. Our CS and procurement teams are looking for clarity on two items:
1) Why did the tier-mapping change happen without notice? We did not apply any config changes.
2) Given the customer impact and lost transactions, what compensation (credits) or SLA remediation will Redwood provide?

We need an executive contact available for the next 2 hours to discuss remediation and contractual impacts. Please escalate accordingly.

—Tina Rodriguez
Head of Platform, Acme Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Tina Rodriguez <tina.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exec attention requested — Acme Health 429 incident (need credits + RCA)

Marcus / Laura —

Looping you in as Acme is requesting executive-level remediation and credits. Summary:
- Cause: temporary misapplied org-level override moved acme-health.prod into Shared Standard tier (lower per-project limits) for ~17 minutes, causing 429 spikes and a retry storm.
- Mitigation: Rishi reverted tier mapping and increased per-project cap; 429s reduced to baseline by ~10:05 PT.
- Customer asks: explanation of why change occurred without notice, formal RCA, and compensation for business impact.

Request: please advise on credit authorization (recommendation: 15% of last month's usage for the affected production org or an agreed SLO credit) and whether we should offer a short term dedicated burst reservation while we complete the audit.

I'll prepare the incident timeline and share the RCA draft for review.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachment(s): acme_429-log-snippet.txt, quota-config-snapshot.png

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>, Tina Rodriguez <tina.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exec attention requested — Acme Health 429 incident (need credits + RCA)

Team —

Thanks for the clear summary. I approve the proposed remediation path:
- Offer Acme Health a 15% credit on May billing for the affected project (ACME-EXP-4392). Finance to draft the credit memo and legal to confirm wording.
- Provide a formal RCA within 72 hours. Rishi, please lead with timeline and the fix to the tier mapping service.
- Offer a complimentary 2-week dedicated burst reservation to bridge capacity while we complete the audit and implement a safety guard.

I'll be the exec point of contact for Acme for the next 48 hours; loop me into any calls. Stephanie — please coordinate procurement messaging and run the credit approval through finance.

Marcus Lin
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
